articles.title: IOC Clears Path for Russia at LA 2028, but Flag and Anthem Still in Limbo
articles.summary: The IOC has provisionally lifted its suspension of Russia’s Olympic committee, a crucial step toward full reintegration before LA 2028. But Russia still can’t display its flag or play its anthem — that decision is pending. IOC President Kirsty Coventry stressed that athletes shouldn’t pay the price for their government’s actions.

articles.title: Scorching Heat Buckles Highways — Is Our Infrastructure Ready for a Hotter World?
articles.summary: A July 4th heat wave caused concrete to buckle on I-97 near Baltimore and a Chicago street. Climate change is driving more extreme temperatures and heavier rainfall, both of which weaken pavements. Engineers say solutions exist but cost more, forcing tough choices about how resilient we want our roads to be.

articles.title: Dred Scott’s Descendant and Taney’s Heir Confront a Legacy That Still Divides the Court
articles.summary: Lynne Jackson, Dred Scott’s great-great-granddaughter, and Charlie Taney, descendant of the chief justice who ruled against him, met in D.C. as the Supreme Court reaffirmed birthright citizenship. The 5-4 ruling showed deep divisions over the 14th Amendment, with Justice Thomas arguing it was meant only for freed slaves.
